input_signals.name: R&D-Restored Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-flow-cheap firms earn higher returns when they remain highly profitable after reversing the immediate expensing of R&D.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding R&D back to operating income mitigates the accounting penalty imposed on firms investing in intangible assets; unreported R&D is economically treated as zero. The interaction favors cheap cash generators with genuine innovation-adjusted operating productivity rather than cash-flow yield alone.

input_signals.name: Expensive Fragile-Margin Penalty
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high sales multiples or weak, unstable gross margins underperform firms that are jointly cheap and durably profitable.
input_signals.reasoning: The maximum operator assigns a low signal only when both valuation expensiveness and profitability fragility are low. Thus the attractive low-signal portfolio requires cheapness to be confirmed by persistent gross-margin strength, while high values identify valuation or fundamental vulnerability.

input_signals.name: Earnings-Margin Repricing Concordance
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high earnings yield and improving operating margins outperform expensive firms whose margins are deteriorating.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the binary trend gate and static profitability cross with a symmetric interaction between valuation and margin trajectory. Cheap deteriorators and expensive improvers remain neutral, while the graded positive and negative tails isolate the economically coherent cheap-improving and expensive-deteriorating corners.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sign( add( sign( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ) ), sign( ind_zscore( winsor( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) ) ), min( abs( ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( ib, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ) ), abs( ind_zscore( winsor( trend( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Protected Enterprise Yield
input_signals.hypothesis: High EBITDA-to-enterprise-value firms outperform when they retain strong asset profitability after depreciation.
input_signals.reasoning: EBITDA yield can make capital-intensive firms appear cheap by ignoring the economic consumption of fixed assets. Post-depreciation profitability acts as a continuous quality confirmation, favoring cheap enterprises whose apparent cash earnings are not primarily compensation for asset wear.

input_signals.name: Debt-Service-Safe Book Discount
input_signals.hypothesis: High book-to-market firms outperform when operating profitability has remained sufficient after interest expense, even during their weakest recent year.
input_signals.reasoning: The three-year minimum of after-interest operating profitability identifies a debt-service floor that helps separate solvent value from leverage-driven distress. Its interaction with book-to-market requires cheapness to be supported by recurring debt-bearing capacity rather than a single strong reporting period.

input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ts_min( ratio( sub( oibdp, xint ), at ), 3 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Overhead-Compression Cash Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High operating-cash-flow-yield firms outperform when their SG&A burden is declining.
input_signals.reasoning: A falling SG&A-to-sales trend indicates improving overhead efficiency and a potential expansion in future operating profitability. This prospective cost-discipline channel strengthens cash-flow cheapness without algebraically collapsing the interaction into another current profit yield.

input_signals.name: Profitability-Drawdown Earnings Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High net-income-yield firms outperform when operating profitability is high and has not fallen materially from its recent peak.
input_signals.reasoning: Current operating ROA is penalized by its drawdown from the three-year maximum, distinguishing sustained profitability from cyclically depressed or deteriorating operations. This tests a profitability-retention mechanism rather than reusing sales multiples and gross-margin stability.

input_signals.name: Margin-Recovery Enterprise Bargain
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high sales-to-enterprise-value outperform when operating margins are both healthy and recovering from a recent trough.
input_signals.reasoning: The profitability channel combines the current margin with its improvement from the three-year minimum, rewarding genuine operating recovery without allowing a still-depressed margin to dominate. Enterprise-value cheapness should be more likely to reverse when low expectations coincide with improving unit economics.

input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Profit Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with substantial cash backing relative to market value outperform when post-depreciation operating profitability remains robust through their weakest recent year.
input_signals.reasoning: Cash-to-market captures balance-sheet valuation support that is not a conventional earnings or book-value factor. The operating-profit floor excludes cash-rich but persistently unproductive firms, making financial slack valuable only when paired with a durable operating franchise.

input_signals.name: Enterprise Cash Conversion Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high pre-interest operating cash flow relative to enterprise value outperform when they consistently convert gross profit into operating income.
input_signals.reasoning: Adding interest expense back to operating cash flow better aligns the cash numerator with enterprise value. The separate gross-to-operating-profit conversion ratio measures persistent cost-structure efficiency, replacing the prior documented intangible-capitalization construction with an operating-conversion mechanism.

input_signals.name: Profitable Deleveraging Book Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Cheap, profitable firms that are actively reducing debt earn higher subsequent equity returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Debt reduction is measured directly as the change in total debt scaled by lagged assets, avoiding contamination from contemporaneous asset growth or changes in market interest rates. The three-way interaction targets value firms where operating strength is being used to transfer enterprise value from creditors to shareholders.

input_signals.name: Capital-Light Enterprise Value
input_signals.hypothesis: High EBITDA-to-enterprise-value firms outperform when they are profitable and revenue growth is outpacing growth in the asset base.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating ROA establishes current profitability, while revenue growth minus asset growth identifies firms scaling without proportionate capital expansion. This replaces normalized earnings and a repeated profitability floor with a capital-light scalability mechanism that may retain information beyond static FF5 value and profitability exposures.

input_signals.name: Cumulative-Cash Margin Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms priced cheaply relative to cumulative operating cash generation outperform when operating margins remain strong even in their weakest recent year.
input_signals.reasoning: Three-year cumulative cash flow reduces sensitivity to a temporarily elevated current cash-flow yield and represents sustained internally generated value. The operating-margin floor separately requires durable pricing and cost economics, so the construction does not collapse into a single current profit-to-price ratio.

input_signals.name: Fixed-Charge-Covered Earnings Value

input_signals.reasoning: Operating profit before depreciation relative to interest plus depreciation measures coverage of financing costs and recurring asset consumption. input_signals.name: Ex-Cash Operating Franchise Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose operating businesses are cheap after stripping out cash outperform when their noncash operating assets generate strong profits.
input_signals.reasoning: Removing cash from book equity, market value, and total assets isolates the valuation and profitability of the operating franchise rather than rewarding cash holdings themselves. The matched construction requires the ex-cash business to be both inexpensive and productive, replacing the archived enterprise-cash conversion mechanism.

input_signals.reasoning: Profitability level and acceleration are ranked separately before taking their minimum, giving acceleration equal cross-sectional influence instead of allowing its smaller numerical scale to disappear. The quality score can be high only when both the level and change-of-change dimensions are strong, making this a genuine acceleration-conditioned value signal.

input_signals.reasoning: Cash net of current debt measures near-term funding capacity rather than reusing the low-alpha EBITDA-to-enterprise-value leg. input_signals.name: Cash-Burn-Protected Balance Value

input_signals.reasoning: The weaker of post-depreciation operating ROA and cash ROA determines whether balance-sheet cash is supported by a self-sustaining business. This directly filters cash-rich firms that are consuming liquidity, using current dual-channel profitability rather than another temporal floor.

input_signals.name: Overhead-Productive Enterprise Sales Value
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high sales-to-enterprise-value outperform when they consistently generate substantial operating income per dollar of SG&A.
input_signals.reasoning: Operating income relative to SG&A measures the productivity of overhead and organizational spending rather than merely tracking a declining expense ratio. Requiring reliable overhead productivity may avoid the fragile turnaround firms that weakened prior sales-to-enterprise-value recovery portfolios.

input_signals.reasoning: Debt reduction scaled by market capitalization measures the potential transfer of enterprise value from creditors to shareholders rather than another level of balance-sheet cash. input_signals.reasoning: Scaling the fixed-charge surplus by assets avoids the explosive denominator of an operating-profit-to-fixed-charge coverage ratio.
